Azjakuma (Y01)

Survey-table region: Haless.

In one sentence: From the fortress-temples of the Demon Hills in Haless, the Horned Ogre nation builds a fearsome demonic empire through the Devouring Path, its mage estate, and the draining of spiritual energy.

Story: Very high | Mission tree: Long (61 direct missions) | Mission-tree update: exact date unverified; local version v1.37.5.0 | Distinctiveness: Very high | Tedium: High | Early pressure: High | Expansion: Very high.

Ancient Fortress-Temples in the Demon Hills

In 1444, Azjakuma is already an established theocracy of Horned Ogre culture and the Devouring Path faith, with its unique Tagharoghi reform. The history file names Tiraga Aromo as ruler and Akira Surgoshi as heir, and also sets several hostile and friendly relations with neighboring states. “Chomora” should not be mistaken for the starting country name: it is a possible later change to the regime and displayed name of the same Tag as the mission tree advances. [Local history script]

The offline English Wiki traces Azjakuma's origins to a failed revolt by ancient Stone Ogres against the giants: after a rebellion around 7325 BA, the exiles migrated to the Demon Hills; Dwarven records place the name “Azjakuma” around 7250 BA. Since then, Azjakuma has relied on its mountain-top fortress-temples, which serve at once as libraries, fortresses, and religious centers, to preserve a tradition of knowledge and military strength in relative isolation. The Wiki itself presents the origins of spiritual siphoning as uncertain, so its precise account should not be treated as undisputed history. [Wiki]

This is a country shaped jointly by the preservation of knowledge and the taking of power: ancient archives, mages, corrupted temples, and spiritual energy are all bound up with its expansion. An early official development diary listed Azjakuma and the Demon Empire among planned content; a 2024 Devouring Path diary described changes to that religion's design. What is playable now, however, must be established from the local mission and event scripts. [Local Mod] [Official development diaries]

From Azjakuma to Chomora

The 61 direct missions are not simply a straight conquest of Haless. The early stage first develops Azjakuma itself—its mountain infrastructure, border strength, mages, and military organization—then turns toward establishing subjects and controlling strategic nodes. The pivotal mission Y01_way_forward triggers a dedicated event. If the player reaches that route, the event can rename the country “Chomora” (CHOMORA) while keeping the Y01 Tag, change it to a monarchy, and activate the next mission phase. This is a continuation of the same country, not the sudden formation of a separate Tag. Other Tag changes in the scripts must be read in context; a search hit alone does not show that Azjakuma itself changes Tag. [Local scripts]

The later missions push this state toward a much wider sphere: subjects and military conquest extend its reach across Haless, while the route pursues High Temples, spiritual energy, mage rituals, life-extension magic, and the Devouring Path. The missions and events offer a possible future in which the lives of subjects and captives are used to sustain hegemonic power. This is not a completed world state in 1444, nor is it the canonical outcome of every possible campaign branch. [Local scripts]

The Wiki's later chronology also needs a clear boundary. It recounts Azjakuma refusing to send tribute to The Command in 1489 and being conquered in 1492, followed much later by the use of High Temples in bringing about the Rending. This is one setting-history timeline, not a guaranteed outcome for every player; the local playable mission tree allows a different result. The two retrieved Wiki pages phrase the outcome differently: the Azjakuma page says The Command demanded full subjugation, while the Horned Ogre page says the Oni submitted as a slave state. This is a source discrepancy, not a revision of the Chinese-source conclusion. [Wiki] [Local scripts]

What Drives the Campaign

First, fortress-temples and defensive terrain. Azjakuma is not an ordinary lowland empire: mountains, temples, costly infrastructure, and powerful neighbors all shape the opening. Player discussions differ: some advocate using forts to advance steadily, while others emphasize dealing with the threat from The Command as quickly as possible. Neither is an established single best route; these are version-bound experiences only. [Local scripts] [Community views]

Second, mages and the Devouring Path. Azjakuma has several mission lines involving magic, siphoning, and the corruption of High Temples. Event text explicitly describes effects made using the souls of prisoners and debtors or the lives of defenders. These are not merely dark atmosphere or a consequence of being ogres; they are concrete harms supported by the text and directly relevant to the country's values assessment. Spiritual resources, longevity, and state power are intertwined, making the campaign more distinctive than a conventional conquest route. [Local event text] [Local scripts]

Third, a two-stage change of government. Moving from Tagharoghi rule to Chomora changes the government, mission setup, and narrative scale. The player must manage both the initial effort to secure a foothold and the later pace of imperial expansion. It suits players who enjoy mountain defense, sinister magic, and a long, multi-stage conquest; it is a poor fit for those who dislike rapid expansion, subject management, or brutal storylines. [Local scripts]

Personality, Assessment, and Evidence Boundaries

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansion 94/100 | Autocracy 96/100 | Magic ↔ Artifice 98/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 97/100) | Pluralism 9/100. Its v2.1 values assessment is Evil (7/100), with a trajectory of radicalization. This is not based on “ogres,” the name of the Devouring Path, warfare, or monarchy. It rests on scripts and narrative text depicting the siphoning of souls from captives, debtors, defenders, and ordinary inhabitants, alongside religious coercion and the treatment of their lives as state resources. The degree of these harms depends on how far the player follows the route, so the score describes the main tendency of the currently documented storyline rather than condemning every possible player action. [Local scripts] [Local event text]

Player posts reflect concerns about strong early opponents, the use of defensive terrain, and disagreements over the route, but they do not establish current rewards or an optimal army composition. Source tiers for the missions, Wiki chronology, and community views are set out in the evidence page.

National Ideas (Reference Appendix)

The following reproduces the current local national-idea text and scripted effects. Traditions apply when this idea set is active; the seven ideas unlock in sequence as the set is invested in; the ambition applies after all seven are unlocked. Only national ideas are listed—racial, government, and mission rewards are not folded into these figures. A later idea set does not automatically stack with the earlier one. Idea descriptions may recount history or express future aspirations; they do not by themselves mean that those events have already happened by 1444.

Azjakuma (Y01) — Oni Ideas

Traditions: Oni Traditions

Effects: Stability Cost Modifier: -20%; Discipline: +5%.

Idea 1: Demons of the Mist

The Demon Hills are a twisted and treacherous landscape, full of dangers in the forms of beast, plant, and terrain. This is a land where only the strongest may thrive, and our enemies must face these obstacles should they desire to face us in battle.

Effect: Hostile Attrition: +200%.

Idea 2: We Shall not Budge

Many powerful forces have attempted to dislodge us from our Shirgrii, our castle monasteries. From the ancient human Rahenraj, to the fierce warlord Harimar, and even the mighty Jaher, all have failed. We have been here since they were but tribes with stone tools, and so we shall remain when all they own crumbles under the cruel hand of time.

Effect: Fort Defense: +25%.

Idea 3: Ancient Wisdom

Our land is an unimaginably ancient one - as far as the humans and tiger folk that rule around us are concerned, we have always been here. Throughout the millennia, we have gathered great and expansive archives of documents, treatises, and various other records. Our monks spend much of their time studying, maintaining, and updating these hallowed tomes.

Effect: All Power Cost: -2.5%.

Idea 4: Aingjada Petitioners

Countless humans make the arduous trek through our lands to meet with us, either in an attempt to slay us in some venture to seem 'heroic' or to gather some of our antediluvian knowledge. Either way, all across Haless know of us, and countless stories about our people are spoken across the land.

Effect: Prestige: +1.

Idea 5: Rituals of Repentance

We consigned ourselves to our Shirgrii long ago in repentance for our ancestor's betrayal of their True Giant masters. Repentance remains a valued virtue amongst our people, and we have countless elaborate and extensive rituals to cleanse oneself of their sins and regrets.

Effects: Devotion: +1; Legitimacy: +1; Horde Unity: +1; Republican Tradition: +0.3; Yearly Corruption: -0.05.

Idea 6: Rage of the Oni

Just as legendary as our wisdom and strength, we are widely known and feared for our incredible rage. While it may be quite difficult to truly infuriate an Oni, the result when one does is a reminder that, without our ascetic ways to keep us civilized, we are truly monsters.

Effect: Shock Damage: +10%.

Idea 7: Waking the Giant

For far too long we have let the world pass us by, locked up in our temples. For far too long we have allowed our enemies to come to us, instead of meeting them on the battlefield. For far too long, we have been denied our destiny by isolationists and cowards. Now, with threats on every side and upstarts at our doors, we shall remind them why one should not disturb a sleeping Oni.

Effect: Land Force Limit Modifier: +20%.

Ambition: Oni Ambition

Effect: Yearly Army Professionalism: +0.3%.
